LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To describe people’s appearance.
MATERIAL
•	 TR#3 Moods Version 2
•	 TR#16 Thief Song
•	 TR#17 Descriptions Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home Song
•	 Moods A5 flash cards
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2)
•	 Days of the Week cards (P.E.M.5)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Purse cutout
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 1: A3 Blank Face (P.3.1) + 
Face cutouts + dice
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 10: Parts of the Face cutouts+ 
Blu-Tack
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Character cards (P.3.2)
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game Reference Sheet
•	 Big Book
•	 Physical traits sheet (A3), stolen Item cards and 
Activities (P.S3)
•	 Dice and Counters (1 per child)
BEFORE CLASS
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
Mission 3. 
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (12’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets 
•	 Moods, TR#3
•	 After School Activities
•	 My Pet

2.– STUDENT STORYTELLING WITH CHANGES (14’)
Today the students can tell the whole story choosing new 
variables. You can also encourage them to get up and act out 
the story, pretending to be the different characters and moving 
around the classroom as if it were a stage.
NOTE: if your group still struggles with telling the story or 
you are short on time, have them tell it without any changes.
3.– ACTIVITY 4: PLAY DETECTIVE (8’)
> How to Play
One S is the detective and has to wait outside the classroom 
while another S (the thief) takes the Purse cutout and hides it 
by putting in their pocket or sitting on it. The detective has to 
find out who the thief is by asking questions.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see if the detective 
can find the thief!”
Choose a thief, have them hide the purse, and tell the detective 
to come back into the room. Use the structure: “Detective, 
detective, come in!”. The detective should ask questions to 
the group to find out who has the purse.
Before starting the round, the group can say, “What does the 
thief look like?” (they can sing this part). Then the detective 
can start asking yes or no questions such as:
•	 Has the thief got long hair?
•	 Is the thief wearing black shoes?
•	 Is the thief tall or short?
Always insist that the Ss ask and answer questions in full 
sentences and structures. Discourage the Ss from asking 
whether the thief was a boy or a girl unless they really can’t 
figure out who the thief is, because doing so may make guessing 
who the thief is too easy.

When the detective is ready to guess, they should ask, “John, 
are you the thief?” and the S being accused should respond, 
“Yes, I am.” or “No, I am not.” If the detective accuses somebody 
wrongly, the thief wins; if the detective accuses somebody and 
their guess is correct, then they win.
> Variation
Once Ss are comfortable playing this game, you can bring 
in some props and have the Ss wear different accessories like 
hats and glasses to make it more fun. This way the detective 
can ask a greater variety of questions.
NOTE: The first few times you play this game, the Ss might 
need your help. Do not hesitate in helping your Ss complete 
some of the sentences or modelling an example and having 
them repeat the sentence after you.
4.– ACTIVITY 1: MAKE A FACE (VERSION 3) (9’)
P.3.1
> Main Activity
Tell your Ss, “It’s time to meet a new friend!”. Use Blu-Tack 
to place the A3 sheet on the whiteboard. Ask your Ss, “What 
is this person’s name?”, and have them choose a name for 
the character. You can write it on the A3 using an erasable 
whiteboard marker.
Each number on the dice corresponds with a face part. Ss 
take turns rolling the dice and choosing one characteristic for 
the character based on the number. They have to answer the 
corresponding question and place the cutout on the A3. 
Here is the target language depending on the number they get:
Hair
T: What is her/his hair like?
S: He/she has got … hair.
Eyes
T: What are her/his eyes like?
S: He/she has got … eyes.

Nose
T: What is her/his nose like?
S: He/she has got a big/small nose.
Mouth
T: What is her/his mouth like?
S: He/she has got a big/small mouth.
Moustache
T: Has he/she got a moustache?
S: Yes. He/she has got a moustache. / 
No. He/she hasn’t got a moustache. 
Ears
T: What are her/his ears like? 
S: He/she has got big/small ears. 
> Follow-Up
Once every S has had a turn rolling the dice, the last S 
should describe the face that the group has created by saying 
for example, “He/she has got long blonde hair, small brown 
eyes, big ears, a small nose, and a big mouth.”
5.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet.
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and 
do the challenge.

•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
6.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
 ACTIVITY 10: DESCRIPTIONS SONG (TR#17)
> Main Activity
Stick up the individual blonde, black, long, short, curly and 
straight hair cutouts on the whiteboard or place them on the 
table before you play the track. For the eyes and mouth, you 
can just use gestures.
Every time you sing “Are you…?” hold up the palms of your 
hands in the air and then point in front of you when you say 
“You”. Then, perform the action as indicated in brackets below.
DESCRIPTIONS SONG
Are you young? 
(smile and imitate rocking a baby in your arms)
Are you old? 
(bend over and walk as if you are an elderly person with 
a walking stick)
Are you short? 
(put your hands down low)
Or are you tall? 
(put your hands up high)
Have you got big eyes?
(point to your eyes and make a big circle with your hands)
Or have you got small eyes?
(point to your eyes and make a small circle with your hands)
What do you look like? 
(point to anybody)
Tell me something more, I’d like to know! 
(point to yourself first and then hold up your hands 
indicating that you don’t know)
Have you got blonde hair? 
(point to the cutout)

Have you got black hair? 
(point to the cutout)
Is it long or short, curly or straight?  
(point to the cutouts) 
What do you look like? I think I know! 
(put your palms facing up then to your eyes and finish 
by pointing to your head)
ACTIVITY 6: INCORRECT DESCRIPTIONS
P.3.2
Joe
> Main Activity
Choose a Character playing card, show it to the Ss and make 
a mistake when describing the character. You can say, “Hmm, 
I think I’m a bit confused...” to make it more theatrical. The 
Ss must correct you by saying, for example, “No, that’s wrong. 
She hasn’t got blonde hair. She has got red hair.” Ss love to 
correct the teacher, so you can make this activity more fun by 
exaggerating your mistakes and acting surprised or confused 
when they correct you.
> For Advanced Groups
When your Ss get the gist of the activity, and they are familiar 
with the target language, you can let them take on the teacher 
role and incorrectly describe a character.
